scenes.voice: What if your code editor was also your studio? This is Strudel, playing live inside VS Code.
scenes.screen: demo.strudel playing in the Strudel editor, the code lighting up, the Mixer below.
scenes.zoom: The whole window, then the lit code.

scenes.voice: Every sound is one click away. Hear it, like it, and it's in your song.
scenes.screen: The Library: everything, then the TR-909, then a search.
scenes.zoom: The Library in the side bar.

scenes.voice: There's a real mixer too. Move a fader, and watch the code change with it.
scenes.screen: The Mixer with the bass unfolded, a fader moving, the number in the code following.

scenes.voice: Got a MIDI controller? Click the little knob, turn yours, and it's mapped.
scenes.screen: A knob button turning red, a knob turned, the button turning green, the slider following.
scenes.zoom: The knob column beside the code, then the slider.

scenes.voice: It even runs synth firmwares from The Firmware Hub, screens and knobs and all.
scenes.screen: 07-vibefm1-obervave.strudel playing, the Devices tab with OBERVAVE's screens moving.

scenes.voice: And your songs are just files. Git, search, Codespaces: it all just works.
scenes.screen: The Explorer with the template's songs and samples, the demo open.

scenes.voice: It's free and open source. Come find it on GitHub.
scenes.screen: End card: the logo, the name, github.com/alienmind/strdltn.
